That used to be my line of thinking as well except for a certain antagonist who I've always thought was the worst and least interesting "villain" ever created. Playing again, there are 2 really cool set pieces which are the plane crash and the ship turning on its side. Other than those 2 parts, the rest of the game is just uninteresting, unbelievable and somewhat annoying. I've achieved the highest level of completion in the game twice and I like to think that gives me an unbiased leg to stand on. It's decided that the main character and his partner will go together to one part of the world while another pair will split off and go together to another part of the world to find a treasure. The first place you go to is a European country to raid some old castle for one half of the treasure you need. Once you find it, the antagonist and his men are there, of course, and steal the treasure from you, leaving you to be attacked by a swarm of giant spiders that exist for some reason (hey, let's put big spiders in there). Then you go to a Middle Eastern country to find the other pair because you have lost contact with them and believe them to be captured. Nope, one character just didn't top up his phone minutes and to make matters more annoying, they've done nothing the whole time you were in Europe. Somehow the antagonist has beaten you there and his men are already in great number. He steals your notebook from one character after drugging him and then that character turns on you. You find the second part of the treasure and everybody decides that it would be safest for that character to carry it (WTF???). It, of course, gets stolen again and you are set upon by millions of spiders... again. In a different part of the world, somehow these spiders are everywhere. Then you go to another location in a different part of the world to find some different treasure which then gets stolen again by the antagonist's men who somehow always know where you are going and once again get chased by... yep, you guessed it, giant spiders (the originality and fresh game design is outstanding). I haven't even mentioned all the annoying scenes where the main character gets drugged and you're running around in a dream state, that's *REAL* fun. And people think the first game in the series is repetitive. Anyway, I could go on all day about what makes this installment a bad game.

EDIT: The grenade throw-back was a great idea and a much-needed implementation, but it wasn't always reliable. A lot of the time a grenade would land at your feet and the prompt to throw it back just wouldn't show up, so you're spamming the button, but nothing is happening and you die.
